statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk 20% sits at the bottom of the watch band while stress stays high at 70%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is WATCH. The narrow evidence-based danger window runs 12:30Z to 15:00Z, covering the August personal income and outlays release, the quarter-end US cash open and Chicago PMI. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: ADP beats at +90k and the August PCE block lands as NQ holds a narrow overnight range into a quarter-end open
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade 30,556.00, down 0.19%, inside a narrow overnight range of 30,512.25 to 30,705.75, after the cash index closed at 30,339.33 on 29 September. The drift lower is shallow, there is no observed repeated extension after failed retracements, and VIX at 16.13 confirms contained realised volatility, so the price path is not currently pathological. The event stack is the reason stress stays high rather than the path. September ADP private payrolls printed +90,000 against roughly +73,000 expected, a modest upside surprise, and the August personal income and outlays report was released at 12:30Z with consensus looking for core PCE to hold near 3.3% year over year; the actual figure was not corroborated across independent sources by the assessment cutoff, so post-release structure is treated as unobserved. The rates complex remains the dominant stress carrier, with the 30-year Treasury yield having crossed 5.6% on 29 September for the first time since June 2002 and the 10-year near a 2007 high around 5.26%, although yields eased in European trade after New York Fed President Williams said there is no need for urgency on an October hike, cutting October hike odds from roughly 70% to about even. Crude is firm, with WTI at 90.32 dollars and Brent at 97.55 dollars on Middle East supply concerns, which conflicts with the easing in yields rather than aligning with it. Ahead lie the quarter-end cash open at 13:30Z, Chicago PMI at 13:45Z, Micron fiscal Q4 results after the close, and the 1 October ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims block. Shared Finviz context was collected at 2026-09-29T23:14Z with partial status and no futures coverage, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used as current evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude Tail risk fell from 21% to 15% before ticking back to 16%, and stress eased from 75% to 65% before firming to 69% into the European morning. The yellow WATCH readings of the 29 September European and US sessions gave way to a steady green EA_ON run from 20:00Z onward. One hour, 2026-09-29T14:00Z, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Dominant mode moved from trend-up and trend-down prints during the cash session to normal and then mixed overnight, consistent with orderly two-way trade rather than sustained one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the 20-21% watch band from the current hour through 15:00Z, covering the August personal income and outlays reaction, the quarter-end US cash open and Chicago PMI, then eases back to EA_ON through the afternoon on the base case of orderly price discovery and volatility decay. A second, smaller watch-band window at 20:00Z to 22:00Z reflects Micron's fiscal Q4 report and guidance call landing in a thin post-close book, where a semiconductor repricing is the plausible delayed second-leg mechanism. Overnight and into the European morning Tail settles at 16-18% while confidence decays from 85% to 72% as the evidence base ages ahead of the 1 October ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims block.
